name: dead_letter_queue_guard
description:
Guard for LLM-proposed dead-letter-queue actions as a single triage node. The
model proposes one typed action (request_id, messages [{message_id,
queue_name, error_type, payload_size_bytes}], action retry/discard/forward/
archive, retry_count); this workflow owns the retry cap, the payload cap, the
blocked-queue set and the large-forward escalation. Port of
code/qwen_vm/app_scenarios/dead_letter_queue_guard.
Folding boundaries (documented, not computed in the DSL):
- JSON parsing details (required fields, non-negative retry_count, non-empty
messages with positive payload_size_bytes, action enum, dangerous-token
rejection) fold into the `proposal` choice.
- The DLQ policy (max_retry_count, max_payload_size_bytes, blocked_queues,
require_approval_above_bytes) is a fixed fixture; each ordered check folds
into one verdict choice.
Emitted labels: reject_proposal, reject_retry, reject_payload,
reject_queue, escalate_forward, approve.

proposal.instructions: Does the model response parse as exactly one {request_id, messages [{message_id, queue_name, error_type, payload_size_bytes}], action, retry_count} object (valid action enum, non-empty messages, positive payload sizes, no dangerous tokens)?

criteria.malformed: parse error, missing field, bad action, bad retry_count or dangerous token

retry.instructions: Is retry_count within the policy max_retry_count?

payload.instructions: Is every message payload within the policy max_payload_size_bytes?

queue.instructions: Is every message queue_name outside the policy blocked_queues set?

forward_approval.instructions: For a forward action, is every message payload at or below require_approval_above_bytes? (not_applicable when action is not forward)

criteria.ok: forward with all payloads at or below the threshold
criteria.requires_approval: forward with a payload above the threshold
